newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan armed rebel group prepares to disband.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan armed rebel group prepares to disband.

text.p: Members of Nicaragua's largest remaining armed rebel group were assembling in three "peace zones" in preparation for demobilization talks on Jan. 15, a government minister said on Tuesday.

Outgoing Social Action Minister William Baez said the government gave members of Northern Front-380, an armed group loosely linked to the former Contra rebels, until Jan. 10 to congregate in these "peace zones" if they wanted to negotiate with the right-wing government of President-elect Arnoldo Aleman that takes office on Jan. 10.

Baez told a news conference that 160 self-styled rebels had already entered camps in the north and central provinces of Jinotega, Matagalpa and Boaco but said there might be some criminals among them hoping to cash in on land or credit given as part of the demobilization pact.
The front, estimated to be about 220-strong, re-armed after a 1990 peace treaty to demand the government fulfil the promises it made to them.
Since 1990, armed rebel bands have killed 1,000 people, wounded 400 and kidnapped 600 civilians, according to army figures.
